recommendations.rationale: Do not select improvement-96f0ade35119 as an overall improvement: the sealed comparison classifies it as a physical_tradeoff and joint acceptance stays false. Reach worsened but still passes; holding position and hold speed improved yet remain far outside their limits; computation worsened. Accepting this diagnostic recommendation is separate from selecting the controller candidate.

Further weight-only tuning of holding_tip_speed_weight is a low-yield lever on this baseline: the 0.0->0.05 change moved sampled holding-window speed in the intended direction but left it about 59x the 0.02 m/s limit. If a further bounded experiment is authorized, prioritize the persistent computation/solve-budget and horizon observations (both unread here) over more weight-only changes, without asserting attribution.

No closed-loop counterfactual replay is available and a single paired weight change with mixed physical effects cannot attribute the reach/holding outcomes to any weight, budget or horizon mechanism; defer causal attribution.

attribution.reason: Both runs record deadline_misses = 35 against the 0.01 s control period while the candidate averages 17.77877309145406 s per complete update, so plan selection plausibly occurs under a saturated solve budget; the paired weight change does not certify this as the cause.

Raising holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0->0.05 with terminal_tip_speed_weight left at 0.0 lowered sampled holding-window max speed by 0.4060100069642385 m/s, showing the term acts in the intended direction, yet the candidate still records 1.1750052670100422 m/s, about 59x the 0.02 m/s limit; an unpenalized hold-speed term is a minor contributor and does not by itself account for the violation.
The adopted change was a weight only; per-update effective_horizon was not read in this context, so this hypothesis is neither supported nor refuted by the new evidence.
Per-tendon force-limit saturation evidence (the force_limit_saturated signal) was not read in this context, so this hypothesis remains untested rather than supported or refuted.
Terminal reach passes in both runs; the candidate terminal error 0.00869890424761182 m sits inside the 0.01 m tolerance, so the failure is not terminal reach.
One paired weight change yields a physical_tradeoff classification with mixed physical effects and no counterfactual replay; no dominant cause is established.

facts.statement: Candidate terminal reach passes: detail.terminal_error_m = 0.00869890424761182 m inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance, with official_reach_task_success = true; joint reach+holding acceptance is nevertheless false.

Candidate sampled final holding window (0.30-0.35 s, 6 samples) violates both settling limits: max world-tip position error 0.05650455971948983 m versus position_limit_m 0.01 m, and max world-tip speed 1.1750052670100422 m/s versus speed_limit_m_s 0.02 m/s (about 59x).

The single adopted design change moved control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight from 0.0 to 0.05 while terminal_tip_speed_weight stayed at 0.0; the sealed candidate-minus-baseline arithmetic is mixed: terminal_error_m +0.001056295661744434 m, holding_max_error_m -0.001633544566242727 m, holding_max_speed_m_s -0.4060100069642385 m/s, mean_complete_update_s +0.5154540428891785 s, classification = physical_tradeoff.
Computation stays saturated relative to the task: candidate mean complete-update time 17.77877309145406 s against a 0.01 s control period, with deadline_misses = 35 in both runs (delta 0).
